question: The radius of the circle is 10 cm and the perpendicular distance from the chord to the centre is 6 cm. The length of the chord is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The radius, perpendicular distance, and half of the chord form a right-angled triangle.

Using the standard (6, 8, 10) Pythagorean triplet, the half-chord length corresponds to 8 cm.

The total length of the chord is simply twice its half-length.

Length of chord = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/18893c01170530378724f90fc3e692cc428fef3e6b41f54d9d9e0ab7c24ae4a8.png] 

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (OB) = 10 cm

Perpendicular distance from the centre to the chord (OM) = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

By Pythagoras Theorem: (Hypotenuse)² = (Perpendicular)² + (Base)²

A perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

**Calculations:**

⇒ In right-angled triangle OMB, OB² = OM² + MB²

⇒ 10² = 6² + MB²

⇒ 100 = 36 + MB²

⇒ MB² = 100 − 36

⇒ MB² = 64

⇒ MB = √64 = 8 cm

⇒ Since the perpendicular OM bisects the chord AB, the total length of chord AB = 2 × MB

⇒ AB = 2 × 8 = 16 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular to a Chord Theorem

A perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord perfectly bisects the chord into two equal segments.

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Knowing core triplets like (3, 4, 5), (6, 8, 10), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) helps in solving right-angled triangle geometry problems instantly without manual calculations.

Longest Chord

The longest chord of a circle passes through its centre, known as the diameter, where Length = 2 × radius.
